newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended a quiet session easier with the market unperturbed by reports of a sharp drop in Colombian coffee production. At the close, November was off $2.00 at $1,480. In New York arabica futures scored moderate gains on speculative and roaster buying. Little impact was seen from the latest round of certified stock figures, released after the close indicating that certified coffee stocks fell by 565 60-kg bags as of September 20. Reports that Colombian January/August coffee production was down 12.8 percent at 6.57 million 60-kg bags after unusually heavy rains earlier this winter had no impact on prices. Most observers remain skeptical regarding the further development of coffee prices and forecast further declines. FUNDAMENTALS

UNITED STATES - Certified coffee stocks showed a limited decline during the period ended September 20. Stocks in New York and New Orleans remained unchanged at 4,811 and 26,990 bags respectively, while stocks in San Francisco increased by 500 bags to 5,750 bags. Stocks in Miami fell by 1,065 bags to 4,551 bags. The total on September 20 was 42,102 bags compared to 42,667 bags on September 13.

COLOMBIA - Colombia produced 6.570 million 60-kg bags of green coffee in January/August 1996, 12.8 per cent less than the 7.535 million bags produced the same period last year, statistics from the National Coffee Growers Federation showed. Production in calendar year 1996 is estimated at 10.5 million bags, down from 13.6 million bags in 1995.

MEXICO - According to the Mexican Coffee Council, coffee exports in August 1996 reached 147,342 60-kg bags compared to 184,486 bags in August last year. That brought total exports in crop year 1995/96 (October/September) up to 4.492 million bags which compares to 3.156 million bags exported the same period in 1994/95.

UNITED KINGDOM - The UK imported 228,870 bags of coffee in June 1996, slightly more than the 228,432 bags imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.507 million bags, 14 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 18 percent to 2.783 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Costa Rica (134,400 vs 189,700 bags), Colombia (135,000 vs 92,700 bags) and Vietnam (166,200 vs 72,400 bags). The country exported 292,600 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 8.5 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by nearly 20 percent to 538,400 bags.
